statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 66 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs 25 to 35 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence declines from 66 to 60 purely because the reference tape ages. No danger window is published, because the first hour in which observable Nasdaq-100 structure can exist falls after the end of this forecast.
headline: Weekend halt, hour twenty-three: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, the 10-year near 4.72% and a coin-flip September Fed meeting after Warsh; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August and the scheduled reopen falls about four hours beyond the final slot of this window. Pre-halt evidence was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range against a 29,695.75 previous close; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant Friday driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: the 2-year yield rose about 12 basis points to roughly 4.38 percent and the 10-year closed near 4.72 percent, while the Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, and September rate-hike odds were repriced to roughly 55 to 57 percent from about 35 percent, leaving the meeting described in current reporting as close to a coin flip. The decline was narrow rather than broad: the semiconductor industry fell 2.91 percent and semiconductor equipment 3.96 percent, led by Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent, while five of eight tracked megacaps advanced, with Amazon up 3.97 percent, Alphabet up 1.74 percent and Microsoft up 1.68 percent, leaving megacap dispersion near 2.5 percentage points. Sector context was split, with Technology about 1.4 percent lower against Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical each about 1.4 percent higher. Commodities were re-verified this run with WTI at 83.44 dollars, down 0.11 percent, and Brent at 88.29 dollars, down 0.26 percent, with no verified new Middle East supply discontinuity; gold remained sharply lower, consistent with a real-rate driven repricing rather than a growth scare. The shared cross-asset context file read this run was collected at 17:56 UTC and is now marginally past its 90-minute freshness bound, so it was used only as composition confirmation for the independently verified Friday session and explicitly not as live price-path evidence; its complete futures, breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections were directionally consistent with that verification. Weekend headline flow through the assessment cutoff has been thematic, dominated by commentary on the Fed's communication and rate path and on AI infrastructure, with no verified geopolitical or policy discontinuity. Because Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path and no venue is open to produce one, Tail is 5 in every hour of this window and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window; Stress runs 25 to 35 in the moderate band purely as a measure of information waiting to be priced at the reopen and ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack that ends with the August payrolls report; Confidence steps down from 66 to 60 as a function of tape age rather than conflicting evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final hour of Friday's cash session, the post-close futures hour, and hours one through twenty-two of the weekend halt. The mode was event/whipsaw while the Jackson Hole keynote was digested, and Tail was 20 with Stress at 58 in the 19:00 to 20:00 UTC block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the mode moved through mixed to normal and Tail decayed to 5, where it has stayed for every hour of the halt. Stress fell from 58 to a 22 to 25 plateau, and Confidence declined steadily from 88 to 67 as the reference tape aged rather than because evidence became conflicting. No hour in the window is unavailable.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress runs 25 to 35 in the moderate band, rising with the stock of unpriced weekend information ahead of a reopen at Sunday 22:00 UTC that falls about four hours after the final slot, and ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack. Confidence declines from 66 to 60, staying in the solid band because the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified even as the reference tape ages past sixty hours by the end of the window.
